SAF and Jet A blending 32 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3.2 New England Jet Fuel Logistics and Airport Infrastructure NLR met with airports, terminal owners, and fuel delivery companies to obtain the data and information shared in Sections 3.1 and 3.2.11 New England’s Jet A is primarily sourced from New York Harbor and Canadian imports (Figure 23). New England terminals storing Jet A are located along waterways and receive the fuel by barge and/or tanker (ship). Large volumes of Jet A are delivered on the Colonial Pipeline from the Texas to New York Habor terminals, where the fuel is offloaded to barges and tankers for delivery to New England terminals. Irving Oil’s New Brunswick refinery supplies New England terminals by barge and tanker. Jet fuel movements by pipeline in the region are limited. Fuel is delivered by barge to Energy Transfer’s East Boston terminal and then by pipeline to BOS. BDL receives fuel from Buckeye Partners’ pipeline, which originates in New Haven and terminates adjacent to Westover Air Reserve Base in Massachusetts. All other New England commercial and general aviation airports receive fuel by truck. Figure 23. New England jet fuel logistics. The arrows show general movements of jet fuel from New York Harbor, Canada, and other imports into New England ports, where the majority of terminals are located. Table 21 shows New England terminals storing jet fuel and total tanks and capacity for all products stored, which includes other products such as transportation fuels, distillates, heating oil, chemicals, asphalt, and additives.12,13 The intention is to highlight the relative size of the terminal for comparison purposes rather than specific jet fuel capacity, as fuels stored change over time with lease contracts. Of the eight terminals storing jet fuel, five supply commercial and general aviation. Energy Transfer’s East Boston terminal supplies the highest volume, as it serves BOS, which consumed 579 million gallons in 2024.
